text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Government still says it is possible to halve unemployment during its term, despite a slow improvement so far and scepticism.
- Justice ombudsman proposes charges for two Finnish army officers who forced seven sick conscripts to join in outdoor drilling exercises in temperatures below 30 degrees Celsius. @

- The popularity of community service instead of normal prison sentences has been higher than expected, with more than 3,000 convicts with less than eight months to serve choosing the option last year.
- Tampere university studies use of cells from pigs' eyes as replacement for some of the hares needed for animal testing in eye research.
- Police fear U.S. citizen charged last week with manslaughter for infecting Finnish woman with the HIV virus may have spread it to tens or even hundreds of women, some underage. @

- Some 54,000 previously price-regulated and government financed so called Arava apartments will be sold on the free market by the year 2000. These can be a good investment, government housing fund official says.
- Merita Bank forecasts Finnish housing production will rise 15 percent this year and 20 percent next.

- Transport industry may save 400 million markka per year when maximum length of combination lorries is raised to 25.25 metres from 22, transport ministry says, adding it is prepared to change laws to that effect from the start of July. @
- Swedish pulp producers' pulp stocks rose by 50,000 tonnes in December, papers' own survey shows.
- The markka has been part of the constitution since 1991 but the euro will nonetheless replace it if introduced, experts say.
- A further tax cut for the low- and medium-earners is needed to improve employment, committee says. @
- Jobseekers can market themselves across the whole country at the labour ministry's website from next week.
